### dkt2d

$\OpenLB$ provides an alternative approach to conventional resolved particle simulation methods, referred to as the homogenised lattice Boltzmann method (HLBM).
It was introduced in "Particle flow simulations with homogenised lattice Boltzmann methods" by Krause *et al.* [@krause:17] and extended for the simulation of 3D particles in Trunk *et al.* [@trunk:16].
It was eventually revisited in [@trunk:21].
In this approach, the porous media model, introduced into LBM by Spaid and Phelan [@spaid:97], is extended by enabling the simulation of moving porous media.
In order to avoid pressure fluctuations, the local porosity coefficient is used as a smoothing parameter.
For solid-solid interactions, a discrete contact model is used [@marquardt:23].

The example `dkt2d` employs said approach for the sedimentation of two particles under gravity in a water-like fluid in 2D.
The rectangular domain is limited by no-slip boundary conditions.
This setup is usually referred to as a drafting--kissing--tumbling (DKT) phenomenon and is widely used as a reference setup for the simulation of particle dynamics submerged in a fluid.
The benchmark case is described e.g. in [@wang2014drafting; @feng2004immersed].
For the calculation of forces, a DNS approach is chosen, which also leads to a back-coupling of the particle on the fluid, inducing a flow.
The example demonstrates the usage of HLBM in the $\OpenLB$ framework as well as the utilization of the `gnuplot`-writer to print simulation results.

The `dkt2d` example uses the same subfunctions as other examples to define the geometry, lattice, and boundary conditions.
However, for the simulation of resolved particles, the desired dynamics model and models for contact between particles and walls and particles between each other have to be set.
These are defined at the very top.

```{.cpp}
//Define lattice type
typedef PorousParticleWithContactD2Q9Descriptor DESCRIPTOR;
//Define particle type
typedef ResolvedCircleWithContact2D PARTICLETYPE;
// Define particle-particle contact type
typedef ParticleContactArbitraryFromOverlapVolume<T, DESCRIPTOR::d, true>
PARTICLECONTACTTYPE;
// Define particle-wall contact type
typedef WallContactArbitraryFromOverlapVolume<T, DESCRIPTOR::d, true>
WALLCONTACTTYPE;
```

After that, particle-specific code is only used in the `main` and `getResults` functions.
In the main function, the particle system and particle manager are defined.
Due to the limited number of particles, this example only uses a single `ParticleSystem`, which removes the need for communication between cores.

After that, the movement model for particles is created and assigned with

```{.cpp}
particleSystem.defineDynamics<
VerletParticleDynamics<T,PARTICLETYPE>>();
```

To catch the contacts between particles and the walls, a contact container is created and the properties for contacts between particles and walls or each other are set.
Then the two circles are inserted by calling their creator functions.

In the time loop, the particle positions have to be updated in every time step, and their contacts have to be detected and processed.

After that, results are written, and the fluid lattice is processed by calling `collideAndStream`.

To get data for writing particle results, it is sufficient to call the `particleSystem.get()` function with the `iD` of the required particle and then extract data from the particle element.
Note this is not possible when using a `SuperParticleSystem`.
